headline: Adding AGT-a5193d19-3 to 1 existing rule(s) changed held-out rule-set recall by +41.0 pp and false-positive rate by +0.26 pp (+19 alerts). Awaiting human review.

advisory.title: Preventing Card Testing: Spot It Early, Stop It Fast
advisory.rights_note: Short attributed excerpts quoted for analysis; full text remains at the source URL.
advisory.excerpt:
Card testing is when fraudsters attempt to validate stolen card details by making $0 or low-dollar transactions.
Fraud tactics are evolving, and card testing attacks are increasingly targeting e-commerce and mobile checkout.
They run $0 or small-dollar attempts at real merchants to confirm a card is active and may retry to fill in missing details (like CVV or expiration date).
Automated testing is the most common.
Many different card numbers attempted in a short time—often from the same IP address, device or small set of sessions.
More failed payments than usual, including repeated CVV or expiration date mismatch errors.
Multiple attempts on the same card or session where only one field changes each time (for example, cycling CVV or expiration date values).
A wave of $0 authorizations or low-dollar transactions used to test cards with minimal cost and attention.

dataset.description: Synthetic card-payments scenario (~3% fraud) with velocity, decline, and card-present features, including a deliberately injected card-testing pattern.
dataset.limitations: Fully synthetic. The card-testing pattern was injected to demonstrate how the workflow surfaces a coverage gap; results do not measure real-world detection.

findings.summary: The advisory details card testing attacks where fraudsters execute automated low-dollar transactions and small-amount authorizations alongside repeated failed attempts to validate stolen card details.
behaviors: Fraudsters attempt to validate stolen card details by making $0 or low-dollar transactions
Automated testing running many different card numbers in a short time from the same IP address, device, or session
More failed payments than usual, including repeated CVV or expiration date mismatch errors
Multiple attempts on the same card or session where only one field changes each time
indicators: $0 or small-dollar attempts at real merchants
High volume of failed payments and mismatch errors
Rapid transaction velocity in a short time frame
testable_hypotheses: Cards with high transaction velocity within 1 hour and multiple declined attempts in 24 hours exhibit card testing behavior.
Low-dollar transactions combined with prior declined attempts identify card validation attempts.
uncertainties: Advisory references IP addresses and device IDs which are absent from the transaction dataset schema.
Simulated merchant gateway error codes for CVV/expiration mismatches are represented via aggregated decline counters.

agent_conclusion.rationale: The advisory highlights card testing via small-dollar transactions, rapid velocity, and high failure/decline rates. While IP address and device ID are unavailable, the rule combining declined_attempts_24h and transactions_1h successfully bridges the coverage gap on the validation split, improving recall from 36.8% to 76.3% with minimal increase in false positives.
limitations: IP address and device ID fields are not available in the dataset schema.
Synthetic dataset cannot capture real-world merchant gateway error codes or exact field-cycling patterns.
